summary: Sulfamethazine was pulled from the market in Germany starting in 1992 [3]. Based on a small computer model rather than tests on people, the drug received a high risk score for the liver and a low risk score for the heart [M]. Similar drugs have also been removed from the market, such as Sulfathiazole due to liver harm, skin harm (dermatological harm), and kidney harm (nephrotoxicity) [4]. Another similar drug, Sulfacarbamide, was withdrawn in Germany for liver harm and blood harm (hematological harm) [5].
